_doc: PLACEHOLDER — R28-1 movement prototype (docs/REINTERP_RESTRUCTURE_R28_2026-07-10.md §2 'conducted movement'). Each node wraps an EXISTING camera seat from src/engine/app.ts's seatPose() — no new seats invented, per the session brief. `marker` is that seat's own floor-projected (x,z) at a small floor y (0.03m) — the disc a player clicks to jump there; it is NOT an invented threshold/doorway spot, a deliberate prototype simplification (flagged in 01_SESSION_LOG.md as a V2 candidate: move the visual disc to the room's doorway/threshold instead of literally the chair). `eras` lists which era keys make the node OFFERED; a node is never shown for the era matching the player's CURRENT seat (runtime filter, not data). IMPORTANT DISCOVERY this session: seatPose(180) — the 'spine' pseudo-seat (door + record wall) — returns the EXACT SAME (x,y,z) as seatPose(0), only a different yaw (it is a turn-in-place, not a distinct floor position), so it is NOT represented here as a node; turning to face the spine stays free look (drag/arrow-key), never a marker-move. This is why E1 (home = r1-desk, yaw 0) shows ZERO markers: the only node valid in 'e1' (r1-desk) IS the seat you start at, so the era-filter's own 'never show the current seat' rule empties the list — matching R28 §2's 'exploration becomes possible' language (E1→E2 is when it opens), without needing to fabricate a second Room-1 destination. E2 adds Room 2 (Vera); E3 adds Room 3 (Maya) and Room 1 stays reachable (rooms explored earlier remain explorable forward, per R28 §2's 'the others stay explorable'); E4 keeps the same three-node set (there are only three real desk seats total, so 'go anywhere' by E4 is already true from E3 on) — this era table is a documented judgment call, not dictated by the data model; Sérgio/Fable can widen or narrow it freely by editing the `eras` arrays here, no code change needed.
